limit_order_match_processing.meaning: a limit order matching (partial or full) is being processed through _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder
limit_order_match_processing.checkpoint: before the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

matched_base_amount.meaning: matched base amount of the limit order match
matched_base_amount.checkpoint: before the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

matched_quote_amount.meaning: matched quote amount of the limit order match
matched_quote_amount.checkpoint: before the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.meaning: the matched base amount and matched quote amount have no overlapping 1-bits (bitwise AND is zero)
matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.checkpoint: before the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

rejected_as_zero_cost_trade.meaning: the legitimate limit order match is rejected as a zero-cost trade
rejected_as_zero_cost_trade.checkpoint: at the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

legitimate_trade_fails_misleading_error.meaning: a legitimate trade fails with a misleading error
legitimate_trade_fails_misleading_error.checkpoint: after the zero-cost validation check during limit order matching

assumptions: The zero-cost validation check is the point at which a legitimate match with both matched amounts nonzero could be rejected as a zero-cost trade.
The matched base and quote amounts are observable quantities of the limit order match at the validation checkpoint.

unresolved.description: The report does not quote the exact zero-cost check expression or its operands, so the disjoint-bits precondition is represented by a grounded Boolean rather than a bitwise predicate.
The report does not specify whether matched amounts are caller-supplied inputs or derived from order state; the symbols are declared as observable match quantities without binding their origin.

limitations: The disjoint-bits condition is encoded as a Boolean because the plan grammar has no bitwise-AND predicate; the report's numeric examples (256 & 255, 40 & 21) are not separately encoded.
The misleading-error wording of the impact is represented by a single grounded Boolean outcome rather than a specific error message.
Caller identity and authorization for triggering limit order matching are not stated by the report and are not encoded.
